title: Optimistic output router with kernel-aware selection and attention-window confidence
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement an optimistic (speculative) decode routing layer that picks an execution path based on kernel capabilities and an attention-window confidence signal, accepts partial outputs when they meet a latency-quality tradeoff, and falls back deterministically when confidence is low.

Scope:
- Router component that inspects model metadata (quantization profile, supported kernel primitives, max attention window) and recent telemetry to select one of: fast-kernel speculative path (low-cost, lower assurance) or full-precision decode path (higher-cost, higher-assurance).
- A lightweight attention-window confidence metric derived from prefill token likelihood distributions + attention-kernel compatibility score.
- Acceptance scoring combining delta-logprob stability (short-term token entropy reduction), kernel-conditioned latency estimate, and prefix-match heuristics.
- Graceful fallback: if acceptance fails within N tokens or latency SLO is violated, route to deterministic full-decode path with KV-prefill hints to avoid redoing work.
- Observability hooks: per-request routing decision, acceptance-score time series, fallback reason tags, and end-to-end latency breakdown.

Non-goals: end-to-end rollout automation (handled by Console rollout APIs), model re-training, or changes to tokenizer behavior.

Success criteria:
- 20-30% p95 latency reduction on conversational workloads with frequent short responses when using optimistic path under production-like load.
- <1% increase in unacceptable hallucination rate on monitored prompt sets (post-eval).
- Clear telemetry to attribute regressions to kernel-selection vs acceptance-threshold tuning.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Initial design review: PM (Jonah V.) asked to clarify how we surface acceptance false positives to SRE; decided to add a ‘fallback_reason’ tag and a short trace span for the acceptance decision.

2025-02-18 - Architecture sync: Eng (Marina) prototyped a kernel-capability descriptor (supports_atomic_q8, max_attention, fused_attention_variant). We agreed router will prefer kernels that advertise fused_attention_variant when prefix length > 128 and tail-latency budget < 60ms.

2025-02-21 - Risk assessment: Research (Devdatta) ran microbenchmarks showing some fused attention kernels degrade long-context token quality on causal-only models; added a compatibility penalty to acceptance score to downweight those kernels for long completions.

2025-02-25 - Implementation note: Prefill KV hints will be stored in-memory on the worker for optimistic attempts so fallback can reuse them without full re-prefill. This requires a short-lived KV cache entry keyed by (request_id, model_version).

2025-02-28 - QA plan: Create a stable prompt set (50 prompts) that historically stresses attention aliasing and measure acceptance-score precision/recall vs. ground-truth full-decode. Add synthetic latency injection to test fallback triggering.

2025-03-01 - PR feedback (Code review by Tomás R.): Suggested simplifying the acceptance formula to avoid product-of-probabilities underflow. Action: switch to log-sum-exp stable aggregation and add unit tests for edge cases.
notes: Telemetry plan must include a live experiment with % of traffic routed to optimistic path and a rapid rollback playbook. Coordinate with SRE to set circuit-breaker thresholds before canary rollout.
implementation_steps: Design kernel-capability descriptor and extend model catalog metadata
Implement router decision function with kernel scoring and attention-confidence stub
Add in-memory KV-prefill hint store and worker handshake for optimistic attempts
Wire acceptance scoring and fallback triggers into request lifecycle
Expose routing/acceptance spans to tracing and add Grafana dashboard panels
Run closed canary against internal eval set, iterate thresholds, then staged production canary
